worker, member of fleet home (hub box at box.example.com:4021) ·
  /etc/caramelo/config.yaml · caramelod socket /run/caramelo/caramelod.sock · edge off

The member group is the fleet's: add, token and join are how a box
becomes a member of a fleet; list, show and remove are what the fleet says
about itself. A machine that has joined nothing is a fleet of one.

show with no name prints this machine's record instead: CPU, memory, disks, OS,
network, cgroups and Docker, gauged at setup and at every caramelod start.

Usage:
  caramelo member [flags]
  caramelo member [command]

Examples:
  caramelo member show
  caramelo member list
  caramelo member add you@second-box


Available Commands:
  join        Join this machine to a hub (run on the machine, as root)
  leave       Leave the fleet this machine joined (run on the machine, as root)
  list        List the machines of the fleet
  show        Print the machine record, or one machine of the fleet

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for member

Global Flags:
      --fleet string      fleet to talk to, by its name in the commander config (default: the app's fleet, then the default fleet)
      --json              print machine-readable JSON on stdout
      --machine string    raw ssh target to talk to, for a machine that is in no fleet yet: user@host[:port], or 'local'
      --progress string   how progress is written to stderr: text (default) or json, one event per line

Use "caramelo member [command] --help" for more information about a command.

3 commands are hidden here; 'caramelo manual --role all' lists every command of every role.
